Subject: Notice of Alleged IP Infringement - Horizon Medical

Kimberly,

Horizon Medical has received a third-party notice alleging that certain functionality in our deployed integration (service provided by Redwood under the MSA and Order Form HZN-1784) infringes patents owned by TriVector Labs. We are treating this as a formal claim notice under Section 7 (Indemnification) of the MSA.

Summary: TriVector alleges that the document parsing module used in our integration infringes U.S. Patent No. 10,123,456. The notice was delivered on 2026-06-26 by counsel for TriVector. We attach the notice and the evidence bundle we received. Specifics are in the attached "claim_notice.pdf" and supporting exhibits in "evidence_bundle.zip".

Request: Please confirm within three (3) business days whether Redwood will: (a) accept defense and indemnity of Horizon Medical for this claim per the MSA; or (b) refuse and provide any alternative remediation/assignment options. If you accept defense, please indicate who at Redwood will assume defense control and provide a proposed counsel contact and budget estimate.

We recognize some matters may warrant further technical context — happy to schedule a short call. Given contract timelines, we need an acknowledgement and initial position by 2026-07-01.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
General Counsel
Horizon Medical
Attachments: claim_notice.pdf, evidence_bundle.zip

Elena — thanks for the heads up and for the documents. We acknowledge receipt of the claim notice and the exhibits.

Short answer: Redwood will review and respond, but our MSA allocates obligations with specific defend/control mechanics and carve-outs. To avoid surprises, we need a bit more detail about the operational scope (which customer-facing endpoints are implicated), any patches Horizon may have deployed, and the exact timeline of discovery.

Proposed immediate steps:
- Redwood legal will do an intake and conflicts check (we expect to have an initial position within 3 business days).
- Please provide the mapping between the TriVector-identified code paths and the deployed feature flags in Horizon's integration (a brief matrix is fine).
- We're attaching our internal evidence checklist to clarify additional items our counsel will require ("evidence_request_list.pdf").

Prelim position context: under Section 7.2 of the MSA, Redwood typically offers to defend and control the defense for third-party IP claims that fall squarely within our delivery of the Service, subject to our right to approve settlements that impose obligations on Redwood. Where Horizon's modifications, combinations, or customer data materially contribute to the claim, liability can shift.

Marissa/Connor — looping you both for redline and commercial impact assessment.

Kimberly Park

Kim/Connor — quick internal notes before we draft any client-facing language. My read on the notice: TriVector's counsel is broad on scope but light on technical mapping. We should pursue a narrow defend/control posture with the following guardrails: 

- Ask Horizon to confirm whether they or any third party introduced the contested parser code or trained models on proprietary TriVector corpora. If Horizon made any custom modifications, that could be a carve-out.
- Propose a redline to the Order Form adding a limited indemnity carve-in: Redwood will defend third-party patent claims "solely to the extent they arise from Redwood's unmodified Service implementation as delivered to the customer."
- Add an explicit cooperation procedure and evidence exchange timeline (we want 7 business days to review materials and 14 business days to propose counsel).
- Insist on a mutual non-waiver of Redwood's rights to seek contribution from other vendors/third parties.

Draft language to propose in our reply (high level):
"Redwood will defend Horizon Medical against third-party claims alleging direct infringement by the unmodified Redwood Service as provided under the Order Form, provided Horizon grants Redwood control of the defense, access to necessary evidence, and refrains from making admissions or settlements without Redwood's consent. Redwood's obligations do not extend to claims arising from Customer modifications, third-party integrations, or Customer-provided training data."

Commercial ask: if we accept defense subject to the guardrails above, Sales will likely need to discuss a 6-12 month support credit or uplift to cover near-term legal spend risk. Connor/Rishi to weigh in on commercial.

Marissa
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
